title: Scientism Vault — Architecture
subtitle: Built from a scan of wiki/ (271 pages), raw/, and scripts/; index current as of the 2026-10-01 pass.
summary: A research vault studying scientism and evidence standards. The core loop: immutable raw/ documents are triaged into 207 source pages grouped in 14 topic clusters; 24 per-disease evidence ladders reconstruct the foundational experiments; a 10-rung causation framework grades every claim by the rung its evidence actually reached, while failed experiments are kept visible in a dedicated register. Epistemic concepts, historical-actor case studies, and a long-form manuscript sit on top; an auto-generated index and lint scripts keep the catalogues honest.

nodes.label: Scientism
nodes.description: The vault's namesake problem: extending scientific authority, methods, or results beyond what the underlying experiments support. Anchored on the Bridges flu-vaccine RCT, whose favorable abstract framing outran its unfavorable sick-day endpoints.
decisions: Consensus and peer review are not treated as truth markers; replication is the strongest marker.

nodes.label: Replication crisis
nodes.description: Rebuilt 2026-10-01 from three anchors whose limits are kept distinct: OSC 2015 (100 psychology studies, 36% replicated), the Amgen cancer-biology report (6/53, unpublished data → stays unresolved), and the 2016 Nature survey (attitudes, not rates).

nodes.label: Inferential leap
nodes.description: The central analytic tool: the move from a narrow observation or endpoint to a broader claim the evidence cannot carry. Applied symmetrically to mainstream and Tier-3 revisionist sources.

nodes.label: Trial endpoints
nodes.description: Trial-endpoint discipline: surrogate endpoints vs clinical endpoints, and inert placebo vs active comparator. Anchored on the pediatric placebo-control audit (18 records, mostly active comparators, at least one saline+excipient trial).

nodes.label: Disputed methods
nodes.description: The disputed-methods cluster: germ theory (explicitly unresolved — neither validated nor globally refuted), virus isolation (a term under dispute), and cell culture ('a method, not a conclusion'; CPE-artifact criticisms recorded as legitimate points to examine).

nodes.label: Pasteur · Koch · Jenner
nodes.description: Historical scientists treated as case studies in the gap between experiment, treatment claim, and later narrative — Koch as the methodological benchmark for causal-proof standards, not a symbol.

nodes.label: Revisionist critics
nodes.description: Contemporary Tier-3 revisionist commentary: used for quotations and dispute structure, never for factual closure; when it cites an experiment, the underlying source is ingested separately.
decisions: Feyerabend and Dubos pages remain un-ingested stubs awaiting primary sources.

nodes.label: Evidence ladder
nodes.description: The cross-cutting framework: ten rungs from clinical syndrome description to replicated cross-method convergence, each naming what it can and cannot answer. Guards against 'endpoint compression' — a result at one rung retold as causal closure.
decisions: 'Virus causes disease' is never one proposition; it is expanded into named disease, virus, design, route, comparator, endpoint, result, limitation.

nodes.label: Inferential leaps
nodes.description: Analysis of how foundational attribution papers get extended past their experiments: artificial-route→natural causation, detection→proof, animal-model→human history, association→necessity, tractability→closure. Worked cases: polio (control), AIDS, influenza, measles, smallpox.

nodes.label: Failed attempts
nodes.description: Register of failed, negative, and non-confirmatory experiments, organized per disease pair as boundary findings (route, host, endpoint, model limits) rather than blanket refutations. Flagship negatives: Rosenau 1918-19 influenza, Sabin-Olitsky 1938 polio.

nodes.label: Audit worklist
nodes.description: The upstream research queue: ~28 disease attributions with audit status (candidate papers logged → ladder started → audit added) and per-disease foundational papers each framed with a 'capable question'. Seeds every ladder page.

nodes.label: Program + manuscript
nodes.description: The research-program overview (34 sources; thesis 'procedural rather than doctrinal', six dispute clusters) and the long-form manuscript wrapping the ladder, failed register, AIDS, COVID, and vaccine-outcome strands in ten sections.

nodes.label: Gutknecht audit
nodes.description: Direct-study audit of the March 1995 Gutknecht AIDS letter's 12 questions. Strongest support on Q7-9 (hemophiliac survival cohorts; drugs/AZT-as-general-cause rejected by chronology and non-recreational cohorts; AZT ethics is population/endpoint-specific). Q4-6 and Q10-12 unresolved.

nodes.label: Vaccine outcomes
nodes.description: Does a specific vaccine improve broader overall health? Centered on the PCV9 Gambia RCT (all-cause admissions and mortality endpoints) against the Bridges flu RCT's unfavorable sick-day endpoints; answers 'not established' where only disease-prevention endpoints exist.

nodes.label: Dispute comparisons
nodes.description: Two dispute-structure maps: the rung-separated ladder standard vs the Tier-3 'no-virus' critique (framed as symmetric overreach — endpoint compression vs generalizing negatives), and disease-prevention vs health-outcomes framing.

nodes.label: Herpesviruses (7)
nodes.description: Cold sores, genital herpes, chickenpox, shingles, infectious mononucleosis, Burkitt lymphoma, Kaposi sarcoma — from 1953 VZV tissue propagation through ganglion-latency studies and daily-shedding cohorts.

nodes.label: Hepatitis (3)
nodes.description: Hepatitis A, B, and C ladders — classed by the framework as its strongest experimental ladders: marmoset propagation and chimpanzee transmission through molecular-clone infectivity.

nodes.label: Childhood (5)
nodes.description: Measles, mumps, rubella, polio, hand-foot-and-mouth: the monkey-challenge and tissue-culture era reconstructed rung by rung. Polio is the framework's control case for tight vs extended inference.

nodes.label: Resp & gut (6)
nodes.description: Influenza, RSV/bronchiolitis, SARS, MERS, rotavirus, norovirus, plus the COVID-19 causation audit. Heavy on failed human-transmission and route-boundary evidence (Rosenau 1919).

nodes.label: HPV / cervical
nodes.description: The association-heavy ladder: HPV16/18 cloning, integration state, the 49,655-woman Manchester progression cohort, PCR-negative retesting (HPV-negative fraction shrinks with every better assay), and the 2026 CIDRAP vaccine review as the intervention rung.

nodes.label: Rabies & smallpox
nodes.description: The severe-systemic pair: rabies (neural spread, egg adaptation, street vs fixed strains, aerosol-route tests) and smallpox (monkey inoculation, egg propagation, contact/aerosol transmission).

nodes.label: HIV/AIDS (53)
nodes.description: Surveillance chronology (1981-82 CDC reports), hemophilia mortality cohorts, transfusion/occupational/vertical transmission cohorts, and the AZT trial set (ACTG 016/019/175, Concorde, Delta, Connor). 2026 additions: chimpanzee-infection boundary studies and ICD cases.

nodes.label: HPV & trials (32)
nodes.description: HPV16/18 cloning through deep-sequencing reanalysis of HPV-negative cancers — plus, mixed in by the index, roughly half non-HPV pages: smallpox/vaccinia growth papers, the PCV9 Gambia RCT, flu-vaccine RCT, and vaccine placebo-control audits.

nodes.label: Herpesviruses (26)
nodes.description: From Weller's 1953 varicella/zoster propagation and Epstein's 1965 Burkitt-culture particles through latent-VZV ganglion studies, shedding cohorts, and the 1994-96 KSHV discovery line.

nodes.label: Hepatitis (17)
nodes.description: Willowbrook human-infection series (1967), Feinstone's 1973 immune-EM visualization, Australia-antigen Dane particles, chimpanzee transmission experiments, and the 1989 HCV molecular cloning.

nodes.label: Resp & enteric (29)
nodes.description: Influenza (9: Smith 1933 ferret passage, Rosenau 1919 failed human transmission), SARS/MERS (7: Ksiazek isolation, Kuiken macaque challenge), respiratory/enteric (13: Chanock RSV, Kapikian Norwalk, rotavirus challenge, enteroid culture). The index interleaves some RSV/HFMD/rotavirus pages into influenza.

nodes.label: Classic epidemics (14)
nodes.description: Measles (6), smallpox/variola/vaccinia (5), polio (3): Enders-era tissue culture, monkey and egg propagation, and early variola inoculation work.

nodes.label: Repl & methods (14)
nodes.description: The replication-crisis triad (OSC 2015, Amgen 2012, Baker 2016), sequencing-bias methods, Illumina error patterns — with mumps and rubella primary experiments parked here because no dedicated index clusters exist for them.

nodes.label: Rabies (11)
nodes.description: Goodpasture's 1925 neural-transmission study, chick-embryo adaptation, street vs fixed strain comparisons, tissue culture, and the aerosol and oral/nasal/tracheal route-boundary experiments.

nodes.label: Germ-theory (11)
nodes.description: Germ-theory and historical-debate sources (8): Koch's methods paper, Rivers' 1937 postulates revision, Fredericks & Relman's 1996 sequence-based update — plus the 3-page misc bucket of unextracted Tier-3 material.

nodes.label: raw/ sources
nodes.description: User-owned source documents at the root of everything: ~34 markdown files plus 2 saved HTML pages and the reprocrisis/ subfolder — historical papers, Tier-3 essays, and the seed Scientism.md conversation. Read-only by iron rule.
decisions: raw/ is never edited; every wiki page traces back to something here.

nodes.label: Index & log
nodes.description: wiki/index.md — the auto-generated catalogue of all 271 pages grouped by category and topic cluster — and wiki/log.md, the append-only operation log (2026-05-04 → 2026-10-01).

nodes.label: Scripts
nodes.description: update_index.py regenerates the index from frontmatter; lint_wiki.py checks frontmatter, wikilinks, and orphans; normalize_formatting.py runs the vault-wide formatting pass; two Gutknecht helpers manage PMID/DOI lookups.

nodes.label: Templates & guide
nodes.description: Page templates for the five categories (source-summary is the canonical source-page structure, updated 2026-10-01) and the vault maintenance guide defining the ingest, triage, and lint workflow.

flows.label: Ingest a source
flows.title: From raw/ document to catalogued wiki page
steps: A document sits in raw/ — read-only, never edited by the wiki.
Classify it: Tier 1 primary experiment, Tier 2 scholarship, or Tier 3 commentary. Tier 3 can open questions but never settle them.
Create the wiki/sources/ page, separating what the source claims, what its experiment is capable of answering, and what the wiki concludes.
Update every materially affected concept, entity, comparison, and synthesis page — e.g. Gottlieb 1981 lands in the HIV corpus and the Gutknecht Q8 chronology.
Run scripts/update_index.py --write to regenerate the index, then append the operation to wiki/log.md.
decisions: All writes go to wiki/; raw/ stays immutable.
A claim is 'supported' only when experiment, endpoint, and result are all named.

flows.label: Grade a claim
flows.title: How a virus-disease attribution gets graded
steps: The audit worklist queues a disease attribution with its candidate foundational papers, each framed by the question it is capable of answering.
The per-disease ladder page reconstructs each experiment: design, sample, intervention, comparator, endpoint, result, limitation.
Each paper is placed on one of the ladder's ten rungs — syndrome description up through replicated cross-method convergence.
Claims that outrun their rung are catalogued in the inferential-leaps analysis (five recurrent leap patterns).
Negative and boundary experiments go to the failed-attempts register instead of disappearing — e.g. Sabin-Olitsky 1938 polio, Rosenau 1918 influenza.
decisions: Rung placement, not verdicts: every rung names what it can and cannot answer.

matrices.title: Source corpus clusters (207 pages, 14 index clusters)
The 10-rung evidence ladder
rows: was a named disease pattern observed
was viral material found in the sample
does the agent propagate in lab conditions
that it caused the original disease naturally
did the host respond to the agent
disease-like endpoints in a host by a route
is the agent recovered after infection
exposure, markers, and disease align over time
does blocking the agent change the endpoint
independent methods converge on one model

rows: Bridges flu-vaccine RCT (sick-day endpoints) · seed conversation

stages.title: Arrive in raw/
stages.desc: A paper, transcript, or essay lands in raw/ — read-only forever.

stages.title: Triage
stages.desc: Tier 1 primary / Tier 2 secondary / Tier 3 commentary; tier caps what the source can settle.

stages.title: Source page
stages.desc: wiki/sources/ page written: source claims vs. answerable question vs. wiki conclusion.

stages.title: Propagate
stages.desc: Affected ladder, concept, and audit pages updated; the claim is placed on its rung.

stages.title: Catalogue
stages.desc: update_index.py --write regenerates the index; log.md records the operation.

notes.text: 271 pages catalogued; the index is auto-generated from frontmatter by scripts/update_index.py, and the lint pass after the 2026-10-01 restructuring came back clean.
Only concepts/replication-crisis carries claim_status: supported. Germ-theory, virus-isolation, and cell-culture are explicitly unresolved; the vault treats 'we do not know' as a valid conclusion.

Index cluster drift: 'HPV and cervical cancer' is a de facto catch-all (~half non-HPV pages, incl. smallpox, MERS, and vaccine-trial records); the influenza cluster holds RSV/HFMD/rotavirus pages; mumps and rubella primaries are parked under 'Replication, methods'.
Feyerabend and Dubos entity pages are un-ingested stubs awaiting primary sources — part of the open acquisition queue from the 2026-10-01 log.
Many source pages are abstract-level records pending full-text acquisition; per-page boundaries are noted individually.
